pianoCheck.safety.note: Turning tuning pins changes the tension on strings that together hold many tonnes of load. Use a proper piano tuning lever (tuning hammer) with a tip that fits the pins exactly; never use pliers, wrenches or socket sets, which damage pins and the pin block. Make very small movements, set the pin rather than bending it, and never raise a string far above its target pitch. Old or rusty strings can break and cause injury: wear eye protection, keep your face away from the strings, and stop if a string or pin feels wrong. Loose pins, cracked pin blocks, very old pianos and pianos far below pitch need a professional.
pianoCheck.safety.technician: For most pianos the best choice is a qualified piano technician. Music Portal's Piano check helps you know when to call one and what to tell them; the tuning aid is for people who accept the risks above.

tuningAid.safety.strings: Old or rusty strings can break and cause injury: wear eye protection, keep your face away from the strings, and stop if a string or pin feels wrong. Loose pins, cracked pin blocks, very old pianos and pianos far below pitch need a professional.
tuningAid.safety.technician: For most pianos the best choice is a qualified piano technician. Music Portal's Piano check helps you know when to call one and what to tell them; the tuning aid is for people who accept the risks above.
tuningAid.safety.title: Before you start: tuning safely
tuningAid.safety.tools: Turning tuning pins changes the tension on strings that together hold many tonnes of load. Use a proper piano tuning lever (tuning hammer) with a tip that fits the pins exactly; never use pliers, wrenches or socket sets, which damage pins and the pin block. Make very small movements, set the pin rather than bending it, and never raise a string far above its target pitch.
tuningAid.step.centre: Play {note} and turn the pin of the centre string until the display stands still. Come up to the target from slightly below and finish with a tiny movement to set the pin.
tuningAid.step.first: Play {note} and tune the open string until the display stands still. Come up to the target from slightly below.
tuningAid.step.muteThree: {note} has three strings. Mute the left and right strings (a felt strip or rubber mutes) so only the centre string sounds.
tuningAid.step.muteTwo: {note} has two strings. Mute one of them so only one string sounds.
tuningAid.step.octave: Play {partner} and {note} together and let them ring. A good octave has no beats.
tuningAid.step.rough: Pitch raise, rough pass: bring every string of {note} up to the rough target shown. Stop at the target; never go above it.
tuningAid.step.single: {note} has one string. Tune it until the display stands still. Come up to the target from slightly below.
tuningAid.step.unison: Remove the mute. Play {note} and bring the second string in until the beats disappear. Do not move the first string.
tuningAid.step.unisonLeft: Remove the mute from the left string. Play {note} and turn the left string's pin until the beats slow down and disappear. Do not move the centre string.
tuningAid.step.unisonRight: Remove the last mute. Play {note} and bring the right string in until all three sound as one, with no beats.
tuningAid.stopAdvice: Do not keep turning the pin. This usually needs a technician's hands (for example a loose pin or a pin block problem).
tuningAid.stopBecause.other: The tuning aid has stopped on this note because something did not feel right.
tuningAid.stopBecause.pinTooLoose: The tuning aid has stopped on this note because the tuning pin turns too easily.
tuningAid.stopBecause.pitchJumps: The tuning aid has stopped on this note because the pitch jumps unpredictably.
tuningAid.stopBecause.willNotHold: The tuning aid has stopped on this note because the note will not hold its pitch.
tuningAid.technician.alsoFix: A technician can also fix loose pins, broken strings and regulation problems the tuning aid cannot see.
